SL-000009.transcript:
Member (Arjun Ahmed): My life insurance premium tripled and nobody warned me.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Hi Arjun Ahmed, Marc Tremblay here — let me pull that up.
Member (Arjun Ahmed): I called two weeks before the renewal date to cancel.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Arjun Ahmed): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Arjun Ahmed): It went from about 250 to 750 dollars a month.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Which policy is this about?
Member (Arjun Ahmed): My term life policy. It renewed this month.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Did you get a confirmation of the cancellation?
Member (Arjun Ahmed): No, I was told it would be processed.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Is the payment still coming from the same bank account?
Member (Arjun Ahmed): Yes, same account.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): If the cost came down, would you want to keep some coverage?
Member (Arjun Ahmed): Maybe, if it's affordable.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the policy billing history and the forms received.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I can see your call from the 17th and the renewal payment taken on the 1st.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The renewal rate is higher because the policy moved into a new age band on renewal.
Member (Arjun Ahmed): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The premium increase follows the renewal schedule in your policy, so I can't change the rate. I can send you the renewal notice and your options, including reducing the coverage amount.
Member (Arjun Ahmed): Nobody told me it would triple.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The notice went out 60 days before renewal, but I understand it's a shock at that size.
Member (Arjun Ahmed): How much would a lower amount cost?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Halving the coverage brings it to about 375 dollars a month. The comparison I'm sending shows a few options.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): To recap: the new rate follows the renewal schedule, I've sent you the notice and a lower-coverage option, and you can decide within 30 days.
Member (Arjun Ahmed): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
SL-000009.narrative_summary: Arjun Ahmed, a Sun Life member, contacted support on a premium or billing case. Agent Marc Tremblay reviewed the policy billing history and the forms received. In the end, it was resolved on this interaction, and the member rated it CSAT 3 (neutral).

SL-000089.transcript:
Member (Fatima Fortin): My pension transfer has been sitting for months and my bank says they're waiting on you.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Hi Fatima Fortin, Daniel Okafor here — let me pull that up.
Member (Fatima Fortin): The receiving institution says they never got anything.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Fatima Fortin): Yes, that's right.
Member (Fatima Fortin): The market's moved since then and I've lost money waiting.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Which plan is the transfer from?
Member (Fatima Fortin): My old employer's pension plan. I left the company in May.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Where is the money going?
Member (Fatima Fortin): To an RRSP at my bank. They say they're waiting on Sun Life.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): When did you send in the transfer request?
Member (Fatima Fortin): In June. I signed everything they sent me.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Let me take a look. I've traced the transfer request and the paperwork on the plan account.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Your request came in on June 14. The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer authorization from the receiving institution, which is standard for locked-in pension money.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.
Member (Fatima Fortin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Fatima Fortin): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer form from the receiving institution. I can't release it until that arrives, but I've sent them a reminder.
Member (Fatima Fortin): So I've lost money because of a form nobody told me about?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I understand. I've noted on your file that you've been waiting since June, so it's visible if this needs a review.
Member (Fatima Fortin): Who follows up?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Retirement services will. I've asked them to call you once the form arrives.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): To recap: we're waiting on your bank's signed form, a reminder has gone to them today, and retirement services will call you when it's in.
Member (Fatima Fortin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Emma Wilson): My life insurance premium tripled and nobody warned me.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Hi Emma Wilson, Marc Tremblay here — let me pull that up.
Member (Emma Wilson): I called two weeks before the renewal date to cancel.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Emma Wilson): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Emma Wilson): It went from about 250 to 750 dollars a month.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Which policy is this about?
Member (Emma Wilson): My term life policy. It renewed this month.

Agent (Marc Tremblay): Yes, the full amount. The refund request is approved and goes back to the same account.
Member (Emma Wilson): Will I get something in writing?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Yes, a cancellation confirmation by mail within ten days.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): To recap: the policy is cancelled, the 750 dollars is on its way back, and a written confirmation will follow.
Member (Emma Wilson): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Leila Campbell): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Agent (Daniel Okafor): Yes. It's approved at your plan's coverage level, and your dentist will get the confirmation today.
Member (Liam Singh): Do I pay anything?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): That depends on your co-payment level. Your dentist will see it on the confirmation.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): To recap: the crown is approved, and your dentist will get the confirmation today with your co-payment.

Member (Tyler Cote): I'm following up again — I want to check whether my plan covers orthodontics for my son.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Tyler Cote, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Tyler Cote): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Tyler Cote): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Good question to ask before you commit. Let me look.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Tyler Cote): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Tyler Cote): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?
Member (Tyler Cote): They gave me an estimate of about six thousand dollars.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?
Member (Tyler Cote): No, this is the first time.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Is the orthodontist here in Canada?

Agent (Harpreet Gill): Orthodontic coverage depends on your employer's plan, so I'm checking your certificate now.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.
Member (Tyler Cote): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Orthodontics isn't part of your employer's plan. I can send you the booklet section, and your plan administrator at work can confirm whether that's changing.
Member (Tyler Cote): That's disappointing.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I understand. Some employers offer a health spending account that can be used for orthodontics.
Member (Tyler Cote): How would I check that?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): It would show under Accounts in the app. I don't see one on your certificate, but HR can confirm.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): To recap: orthodontics isn't in your employer's plan right now, and HR can tell you if that's changing.
Member (Tyler Cote): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.

Member (Leila Roy): I'm following up again — my dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Hi Leila Roy, Marc Tremblay here — let me pull that up.
Member (Leila Roy): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.

Agent (Marc Tremblay): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.

Agent (Marc Tremblay): Has this type of claim been paid before?

Agent (Marc Tremblay): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Leila Roy): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Leila Roy): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.

Member (Owen Kim): I'm following up again — my life insurance premium tripled and nobody warned me.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Owen Kim, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Owen Kim): I already explained this on my last contact.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): The notice went out 60 days before renewal, but I understand it's a shock at that size.
Member (Owen Kim): How much would a lower amount cost?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Halving the coverage brings it to about 375 dollars a month. The comparison I'm sending shows a few options.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap: the new rate follows the renewal schedule, I've sent you the notice and a lower-coverage option, and you can decide within 30 days.
Member (Owen Kim): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
